2	// cmd/deploy-worker/main.go
3	//
4	// AutoMESH-Orchestrator – Deployment Worker
5	// -----------------------------------------
6	// This binary is launched as an on-demand Lambda/ container that subscribes to
7	// deployment events (publish/subscribe, SQS, NATS, etc.) and materialises them
8	// as immutable commands.  For every command we pick the best-fit strategy
9	// (blue/green, canary, hot-swap, …) and execute it against the target fleet.
10	//
11	// The code purposefully keeps external dependencies to a minimum; wiring for
12	// concrete brokers (SQS, Kafka, NATS) is hidden behind interfaces, so the same
13	// worker can be re-used in multiple environments without recompilation.
14	package main
15	
16	import (
17		"context"
18		"encoding/json"
19		"errors"

21		"io"

34	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

41		LogLevel   string `yaml:"logLevel"` // debug, info, warn, error
42	}

46		f, err := os.Open(path)
47		if err != nil {
48			return nil, err
49		}
50		defer f.Close()
51	
52		data, err := io.ReadAll(f)
53		if err != nil {
54			return nil, err
55		}
56	
57		var cfg Config
58		if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &cfg); err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61		if cfg.WorkerPool <= 0 {
62			cfg.WorkerPool = 4
63		}
64		if cfg.LogLevel == "" {
65			cfg.LogLevel = "info"

68	}

71	// Domain Model
72	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

74	// DeployCommand is the canonical event consumed by the worker.
75	type DeployCommand struct {
76		ID           string            `json:"id"`
77		App          string            `json:"app"`
78		Version      string            `json:"version"`
79		Tactic       string            `json:"tactic"` // bluegreen, canary, rolling …

85	// Event Broker Abstractions
86	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	
88	// Consumer exposes a minimal pull-based subscription API.
89	//
90	// (Push-based/stream callbacks can be easily adapted internally.)
91	type Consumer interface {
92		Recv(ctx context.Context) (*DeployCommand, AckFunc, error)
93		Close() error
94	}
95	
96	// AckFunc acknowledges or negatively acknowledges processing.
97	//
98	// Implementations usually wrap message brokers’ native ack/nack semantics.
99	type AckFunc func(success bool) error
100	
101	// InMemoryConsumer is a test-double used in CI and unit tests.  Production
102	// deployments replace this with real implementations (Kafka, SQS, NATS,…).
103	type InMemoryConsumer struct {
104		stream chan *DeployCommand
105	}
106	
107	func NewInMemoryConsumer(buf int) *InMemoryConsumer {
108		return &InMemoryConsumer{stream: make(chan *DeployCommand, buf)}
109	}
110	
111	// Recv implements Consumer.
112	func (c *InMemoryConsumer) Recv(ctx context.Context) (*DeployCommand, AckFunc, error) {
113		select {
114		case <-ctx.Done():
115			return nil, nil, ctx.Err()
116		case msg, ok := <-c.stream:
117			if !ok {
118				return nil, nil, io.EOF
119			}
120			ack := func(success bool) error {

123			}

126	}

135	// Strategy Pattern
136	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

138	// DeploymentStrategy selects the appropriate orchestration workflow.
139	type DeploymentStrategy interface {
140		Execute(ctx context.Context, cmd *DeployCommand) error
141	}

144	type BlueGreenStrategy struct {

146	}

148	func (s *BlueGreenStrategy) Execute(ctx context.Context, cmd *DeployCommand) error {
149		s.logger.Info("starting blue/green deployment", zap.String("app", cmd.App), zap.String("version", cmd.Version))

162		if err := s.swapTraffic(ctx, cmd); err != nil {

171		// Simulate provisioning time.

174			return ctx.Err()
175		case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
176		}
177		return nil
178	}

187	}

190		select {
191		case <-ctx.Done():
192			return ctx.Err()
193		case <-time.After(500 * time.Millisecond):
194		}
195		return nil
196	}

198	// CanaryStrategy gradually rolls out the new version.
199	type CanaryStrategy struct {
200		logger *zap.Logger
201	}
202	
203	func (s *CanaryStrategy) Execute(ctx context.Context, cmd *DeployCommand) error {
204		s.logger.Info("starting canary deployment", zap.String("app", cmd.App), zap.String("version", cmd.Version))
205	
206		steps := []int{10, 25, 50, 100}
207		for _, pct := range steps {
208			if err := s.shiftTraffic(ctx, cmd, pct); err != nil {
209				return err
210			}
211			if err := s.monitor(ctx, cmd, pct); err != nil {
212				return err
213			}
214		}
215		s.logger.Info("canary deployment finished", zap.String("commandID", cmd.ID))
216		return nil
217	}
218	
219	func (s *CanaryStrategy) shiftTraffic(ctx context.Context, cmd *DeployCommand, pct int) error {
220		s.logger.Info("shifting traffic", zap.Int("percent", pct))
221		select {
222		case <-ctx.Done():
223			return ctx.Err()
224		case <-time.After(800 * time.Millisecond):
225		}
226		return nil
227	}
228	
229	func (s *CanaryStrategy) monitor(ctx context.Context, cmd *DeployCommand, pct int) error {
230		s.logger.Info("monitoring traffic", zap.Int("percent", pct))
231		select {
232		case <-ctx.Done():
233			return ctx.Err()
234		case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
235		}
236		return nil
237	}

239	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
240	// Worker
241	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
242	
243	// Worker fetches DeployCommands from Consumer and executes them with the
244	// strategy that best fits the “tactic” field.
245	type Worker struct {
246		log        *zap.Logger
247		consumer   Consumer
248		strategies map[string]DeploymentStrategy
249	
250		pool int
251		wg   sync.WaitGroup
252	}
253	
254	func NewWorker(log *zap.Logger, consumer Consumer, pool int) *Worker {
255		return &Worker{
256			log:      log,
257			consumer: consumer,
258			pool:     pool,
259			strategies: map[string]DeploymentStrategy{
260				"bluegreen": &BlueGreenStrategy{logger: log},
261				"canary":    &CanaryStrategy{logger: log},
262			},
263		}
264	}
265	
266	func (w *Worker) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
267		w.log.Info("worker started", zap.Int("concurrency", w.pool))
268	
269		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
270		defer cancel()
271	
272		// Fan-out pool
273		for i := 0; i < w.pool; i++ {
274			w.wg.Add(1)
275			go func(id int) {
276				defer w.wg.Done()
277				w.runLoop(ctx, id)
278			}(i)
279		}
280	
281		// Wait for cancellation.
282		<-ctx.Done()
283		w.wg.Wait()
284		return ctx.Err()
285	}
286	
287	func (w *Worker) runLoop(ctx context.Context, id int) {
288		w.log.Debug("worker thread online", zap.Int("thread", id))
289	
290		for {
291			cmd, ack, err := w.consumer.Recv(ctx)
292			if err != nil {
293				if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
294					w.log.Warn("consumer closed, exiting thread", zap.Int("thread", id))
295					return
296				}
297				if ctx.Err() != nil {
298					return
299				}
300				w.log.Error("failed to receive message", zap.Error(err))
301				continue
302			}
303	
304			if err := w.handle(ctx, cmd); err != nil {
305				w.log.Error("command failed", zap.String("commandID", cmd.ID), zap.Error(err))
306				_ = ack(false)
307				continue
308			}
309			_ = ack(true)
310		}
311	}
312	
313	func (w *Worker) handle(ctx context.Context, cmd *DeployCommand) error {
314		strategy := w.strategies[cmd.Tactic]
315		if strategy == nil {
316			return errors.New("no strategy for tactic: " + cmd.Tactic)
317		}
318	
319		w.log.Info("processing command",
320			zap.String("id", cmd.ID),
321			zap.String("app", cmd.App),
322			zap.String("version", cmd.Version),
323			zap.String("tactic", cmd.Tactic),
324		)
325	
326		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Minute)
327		defer cancel()
328	
329		return strategy.Execute(ctx, cmd)
330	}

343		case "warn":

347		default:
348			cfg.Level = zap.NewAtomicLevelAt(zap.InfoLevel)
349		}
350		return cfg.Build()
351	}
352

354	// Bootstrap
355	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
356	
357	func main() {
358		var (
359			configPath = flag.String("config", "deploy-worker.yaml", "Path to YAML configuration")
360		)
361		flag.Parse()
362	
363		cfg, err := loadConfig(*configPath)
364		if err != nil {
365			panic("failed to load config: " + err.Error())
366		}
367	
368		logger, err := newLogger(cfg.LogLevel)
369		if err != nil {
370			panic("failed to init logger: " + err.Error())
371		}
372		defer logger.Sync()
373	
374		// Example: In production wire a Kafka/NATS/SQS consumer here.
375		consumer := NewInMemoryConsumer(100)
376	
377		// For demonstration push a sample message.
378		go func() {
379			sample := &DeployCommand{
380				ID:           "cmd-001",
381				App:          "checkout-service",
382				Version:      "v1.42.0",
383				Tactic:       "bluegreen",
384				TargetGroups: []string{"prod-eu-1"},
385			}
386			b, _ := json.Marshal(sample)
387			logger.Info("publishing sample message", zap.ByteString("payload", b))
388			consumer.stream <- sample
389		}()

391		worker := NewWorker(logger, consumer, cfg.WorkerPool)
392	
393		// Handle Ctrl-C gracefully.

399		}
400	}

3	// state-change events propagated by the AutoMESH-Orchestrator control-plane.
4	//
5	// The AuditLogger defined in this file is responsible for persisting an
6	// immutable audit trail of every significant automation event that flows
7	// through the mesh.  Each record is formatted as structured JSON so that it
8	// can be shipped to log back-ends such as CloudWatch, Loki, or Elasticsearch
9	// without additional transformation.
10	package observer
11	
12	import (
13		"bufio"
14		"context"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"io"
19		"os"
20		"path/filepath"

25		"go.uber.org/zap"
26		"go.uber.org/zap/zapcore"
27	)

29	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	//                          Public Event Definitions
31	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	
33	// EventType enumerates all event kinds that can be audited.
34	type EventType string
35	
36	const (
37		EventTypeDeploy   EventType = "DEPLOY"
38		EventTypePatch    EventType = "PATCH"
39		EventTypeScale    EventType = "SCALE"
40		EventTypeBackup   EventType = "BACKUP"
41		EventTypeRestore  EventType = "RESTORE"
42		EventTypeSecurity EventType = "SECURITY_SCAN"
43		EventTypeCustom   EventType = "CUSTOM"
44	)
45	
46	// MeshEvent is the canonical event envelope propagated by the
47	// AutoMESH-Orchestrator observer fan-out.
48	type MeshEvent struct {
49		ID        string            `json:"id"`
50		Type      EventType         `json:"type"`
51		Timestamp time.Time         `json:"timestamp"`
52		Source    string            `json:"source"`
53		Payload   json.RawMessage   `json:"payload,omitempty"`
54		Metadata  map[string]string `json:"metadata,omitempty"`
55	}
56	
57	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	//                        Observer Interface Definition
59	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
60	
61	// Observer implements the classic Observer pattern.  Each Observer receives
62	// system events through Notify and may perform side-effects (store, alert,
63	// mutate, broadcast, etc.).  Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.
64	type Observer interface {
65		// Name returns a unique, human-readable identifier for this observer.
66		Name() string
67		// Notify delivers an event to the observer.  Notify must be non-blocking
68		// to avoid head-of-line blocking the primary event bus.
69		Notify(ctx context.Context, evt MeshEvent) error
70		// Shutdown flushes all in-flight data and releases resources.  The caller
71		// should provide a context with appropriate timeout.
72		Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
73	}

75	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
76	//                           Audit Logger
77	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	
79	// AuditEntry is the on-disk representation of a MeshEvent.  It contains extra
80	// book-keeping fields (sequence, recorded_at) that are generated by the
81	// AuditLogger and are not part of the original event payload.
82	type AuditEntry struct {
83		Sequence   uint64            `json:"sequence"`     // monotonically increasing ledger ID
84		RecordedAt time.Time         `json:"recorded_at"`  // wall-clock time at which the entry was persisted
85		EventID    string            `json:"event_id"`     // MeshEvent.ID
86		EventType  EventType         `json:"event_type"`   // MeshEvent.Type
87		Timestamp  time.Time         `json:"timestamp"`    // MeshEvent.Timestamp
88		Source     string            `json:"source"`       // MeshEvent.Source
89		Payload    json.RawMessage   `json:"payload"`      // MeshEvent.Payload

91	}

93	// auditWriter defines the pluggable storage engine used by AuditLogger.
94	// Implementations MUST be goroutine-safe.
95	type auditWriter interface {
96		Write(ctx context.Context, entry AuditEntry) error
97		Sync() error
98		Close() error

101	// AuditLogger is a high-throughput, non-blocking observer that translates mesh
102	// events into immutable ledger entries.  Entries are first buffered in memory
103	// (bounded channel) and then flushed to the underlying auditWriter on a
104	// dedicated goroutine to guarantee that Notify is non-blocking.
105	type AuditLogger struct {
106		name        string
107		log         *zap.Logger
108		writer      auditWriter
109		seq         *atomic.Uint64

117	// NewAuditLogger constructs a new AuditLogger that persists audit entries under
118	// the supplied directory.  If dir does not exist it will be created.  Ledger
119	// files are rotated daily with an ISO-8601 date suffix.
120	//
121	//	./audit/2024-07-19.jsonl
122	//
123	// The logger parameter may be nil; in that case a production zap.Logger will
124	// be created automatically.  bufferSize controls the number of in-flight
125	// entries before producers are back-pressured.
126	func NewAuditLogger(
127		dir string,
128		bufferSize int,
129		logger *zap.Logger,
130	) (*AuditLogger, error) {
131		if bufferSize <= 0 {
132			return nil, errors.New("bufferSize must be > 0")
133		}
134		if dir == "" {
135			dir = "./audit"
136		}
137		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o750); err != nil {
138			return nil, fmt.Errorf("mkdir audit dir: %w", err)
139		}
140		if logger == nil {
141			var err error
142			logger, err = zap.NewProduction()
143			if err != nil {
144				return nil, fmt.Errorf("init zap logger: %w", err)
145			}
146		}

148		writer, err := newRotatingFileWriter(dir, logger)
149		if err != nil {
150			return nil, err
151		}
152	
153		al := &AuditLogger{
154			name:       "audit_logger",
155			log:        logger.Named("audit_logger"),
156			writer:     writer,
157			seq:        atomic.NewUint64(0),
158			queue:      make(chan AuditEntry, bufferSize),
159			shutdownCh: make(chan struct{}),
160		}
161		al.wg.Add(1)
162		go al.run()
163	
164		return al, nil
165	}

167	// Name implements Observer.
168	func (al *AuditLogger) Name() string { return al.name }

170	// Notify implements Observer.  The call is non-blocking unless the internal
171	// buffer is full, in which case the caller will be blocked until space is
172	// available or the context is canceled.
173	func (al *AuditLogger) Notify(ctx context.Context, evt MeshEvent) error {
174		entry := AuditEntry{
175			Sequence:   al.seq.Inc(),
176			RecordedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
177			EventID:    evt.ID,
178			EventType:  evt.Type,
179			Timestamp:  evt.Timestamp,
180			Source:     evt.Source,
181			Payload:    evt.Payload,
182			Metadata:   evt.Metadata,
183		}
184	
185		select {
186		case al.queue <- entry:
187			return nil
188		case <-ctx.Done():
189			return ctx.Err()
190		case <-al.shutdownCh:
191			return errors.New("audit logger is shutting down")
192		}
193	}

196	// flushed or the context expires.

198		al.mu.Lock()
199		defer al.mu.Unlock()
200	
201		if al.shutdownErr != nil { // already shut down
202			return al.shutdownErr
203		}

205		close(al.shutdownCh) // signal producer goroutine
206		done := make(chan struct{})

209			al.shutdownErr = al.writer.Sync()
210			_ = al.writer.Close()

214		select {
